title: Without the per-body label drive, c28's ringed cells either divide or travel, not both: the world's local kernel drive at mu 0.25-0.75 gives a dense population of ringed cells with clean division (159-167 persistent splits, generation 5-6, 0-3 merges at 256^2) but no lineage that swims 3 BL and divides, and at mu 1.5 the cells smear into travelling bands
summary: c28's ringswim SIBMD claim moves every labelled body rigidly with its mean substrate gradient. The same world has a label-free local drive (drive=kernel: v = mu G_sig*(phi^2 grad S)/(G_sig*phi^2)). labkit scan at 128^2, seed 0, t=10000 (scan/results.txt): sig 3 kills all cells (mu 0.5, 1.5); sig 6 at mu 1.5 and sig 12 at mu 1.5 give fused bands (1-4 bodies, occupancy 0.26-0.32); mu 0.25-0.5 (sig 6, 12) keep 11-17 cells with persistent splits 11-28, generation 3-4 and merge/split 0.06-0.11, but max 1.7-1.9 body lengths. c28's ringtrack at 256^2, seed 0, t=20000: mu 0.5 ring >= 1.5 in 97.7% of cell-frames, 159 persistent splits, generation 5, 0 merges, 4 tracks >= 3 BL; mu 0.75 ring 88.6%, 167 persistent splits, generation 6, 3 merges, 53 tracks >= 3 BL (52 ringed), 0 lineages that swim >= 3 BL and divide (the split parents move a median 0.85 BL). At mu 1.5 (the claim's value) seed 5 at 256^2 forms domain-spanning bands (parent review). So the local drive trades motility for individuality, as in c05's ring-motility trade-off; the label operator is what lets c28's cells do both.

finding.operator: label-free local phoretic drive (Gaussian-weighted substrate gradient, drive=kernel) in place of the per-body rigid label drive
finding.control: drive=label vs drive=kernel at the same seed and grid; sig 3/6/12 x mu 0.25/0.5/0.75/1.5
finding.result: 128^2: sig 3 dies; mu 1.5 bands (1-4 bodies); mu 0.25-0.5 11-17 cells, persistent splits 11-28, gen 3-4, merge/split 0.06-0.11, max 1.7-1.9 BL. 256^2 ringtrack: mu 0.5 159 persistent splits, gen 5, 4 tracks >= 3 BL; mu 0.75 167 splits, gen 6, 53 tracks >= 3 BL, 0 swim-and-divide lineages; label drive (seed 5) 90 splits, 67 tracks >= 3 BL, 2 swim-and-divide lineages

limits: One seed per setting; mu between 0.75 and 1.5 and sig between 6 and 12 untried at 256^2, so a narrow window where kernel-driven cells both travel and divide may exist. ringtrack's 'death' count (1504 at mu 0.75) includes tracker identity breaks in this dense population, so I do not report a death rate. Body lengths are net centroid displacement over a track segment; tracks break at contacts.
